description:
# Compliance ticket for opi-q5k.16

Source check: opi-q5k.16 (stdin-buffer.test.ts audit)

## Gaps

### 1. Empty input
Upstream: `processInput("")` emits exactly `[""]`.
Add to stdin_fsm_test.exs under a suitable describe:

    test "empty binary emits one empty event", %{fsm: fsm} do
      :ok = StdinFSM.process(fsm, "")
      assert drain() == [""]
    end

Verify Elixir's actual behavior first — if it does NOT emit anything for empty input, this may be a deliberate quirk; document with a comment and keep the test asserting current behavior (with an explanation of divergence).

### 2. Destroy-time cleanup
Add:

    test "buffer is cleared when GenServer stops" do
      {:ok, pid} = StdinFSM.start_link(subscriber: self(), flush_ms: 20)
      :ok = StdinFSM.process(pid, "\e[<35")
      assert StdinFSM.get_buffer(pid) == "\e[<35"
      GenServer.stop(pid)
      # No assertion needed on buffer (process gone) — key assertion below
      refute_receive {:stdin_event, _}, 50
    end

    test "pending timeout does not emit after stop" do
      {:ok, pid} = StdinFSM.start_link(subscriber: self(), flush_ms: 20)
      :ok = StdinFSM.process(pid, "\e[<35")
      GenServer.stop(pid)
      refute_receive {:stdin_event, _}, 50
    end

### 3. Bracketed paste API — decision required

Upstream emits a distinct `paste` event whose payload is the *content* between `\e[200~` and `\e[201~`; data events are suppressed for both markers AND content during a paste:

    processInput("\e[200~hello world\e[201~")
    // emittedPaste == ["hello world"]
    // emittedSequences == []

Elixir's current StdinFSM emits the markers + content as individual data events (marker sequences + per-grapheme content), and callers reconstruct paste text from the stream. Evidence in stdin_fsm_test.exs "complete paste in one chunk", "paste with unicode content", "paste with newlines", "input before and after paste markers".

Decide: **A** (port) or **B** (document divergence). Do not half-implement.

**Path A — port:**
- Add a `subscribe_paste(pid, caller_pid)` (or include paste events in the existing subscriber stream tagged as `{:stdin_paste, binary}`).
- When the FSM encounters `\e[200~`, enter paste mode — buffer content without emitting events, until `\e[201~` closes; emit a single paste event with the accumulated content.
- Add 5 upstream tests to stdin_fsm_test.exs:
  - complete paste: processInput full string → `{:stdin_paste, "hello world"}` exactly once, no `:stdin_event`s for content or markers.
  - paste in chunks: start-marker alone emits nothing; content alone emits nothing; end-marker completes and emits paste event.
  - input before / after paste: "a" + full paste + "b" → `[{:stdin_event, "a"}, {:stdin_paste, "pasted"}, {:stdin_event, "b"}]`.
  - paste with newlines: accumulated text preserves `\n`.
  - paste with unicode 🎉: accumulated text preserves unicode.

**Path B — document divergence:**
- Add a moduledoc note in `OctoPi.TUI.StdinFSM` that bracketed paste markers are delivered as regular data events and callers must reconstruct paste content themselves, with rationale.
- Keep existing tests; add one "parity note" test that explicitly asserts the current shape (markers emitted as sequences; content as graphemes).

## Re-comparison (required)

After gaps close, re-read tmp/pi-mono/packages/tui/test/stdin-buffer.test.ts top-to-bottom and confirm every upstream `it(...)` block has either an Elixir equivalent or a documented intentional divergence. Post a final comment here before closing.

## Deps
Blocks opi-q5k.1 (acceptance gate).

comments.text: Done. Path B (document divergence) chosen. StdinFSM moduledoc records the rationale for keeping paste markers as data events. Added empty-input and lifecycle cleanup tests. Upstream paste-event tests are intentionally N/A.

title: Port stdin-buffer.test.ts gaps: empty-input, destroy cleanup, decide paste event API
